subject: Segmented debug trace retention request — Arcadia incident #4231
messages:
From: Tim Pryor <tim.pryor@arcadiahealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: security@arcadiahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary extension for debug trace retention (Arcadia incident #4231)

Hi Markus,

During the post-incident review for Incident #4231 (auth-service outage on 2026-10-29) our SecOps team asked whether Redwood can make a customer-scoped exception to keep segmented debug traces and tokenized request metadata for 90 days instead of the default 30-day TTL. We only need these artifacts for forensic analysis and a short regulatory review; they will not be used for analytics or shared externally.

Can you confirm whether a temporary exception is possible, what evidence Redwood would need (SIG/CAIQ items, keystore handling notes), and what the secure upload/transfer process should be?

I've attached a one-page incident timeline and an internal attestation from our legal team.

Attachments: arcadia-incident-4231-timeline.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if that helps.

— Tim
Security Operations, Arcadia Health
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Tim Pryor <tim.pryor@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extension for debug trace retention (Arcadia incident #4231)

Tim — thanks for the details and for the timeline. We can support customer-scoped retention variance in a segmented store for forensics-only purposes, but a few items we need before approval:

- Exact retention window requested (you mentioned 90 days; please confirm start/end).
- A short attestation that the data will be used solely for incident investigation and regulatory review (signed by your legal/compliance).
- SIG/CAIQ artifacts or a CAIQ mapping showing that the request is limited to debug traces and does not include user PII beyond what is already pseudonymized.

Operational notes: if approved we will:
- Place the Arcadia tenant in a segmented TTL bucket with access restricted to our forensics SREs and your designated contacts.
- Provide a signed exception statement and an export receipt when the window ends.

For file transfer, we prefer your security team upload artifacts to the secure Drive link below (SFTP available on request). Once we have the artifacts, Kim (cc'd) will route to infra for the technical assessment.

Secure evidence upload: https://drive.example/shared/Arcadia-4231-evidence

If you can provide the attestation and the CAIQ/SIG mapping today, I can escalate for a two-business-day turnaround.

— Markus Klein
Senior Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
From: Tim Pryor <tim.pryor@arcadiahealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: security@arcadiahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-02T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extension for debug trace retention (Arcadia incident #4231)

Markus — thanks, and appreciate the clear checklist. Confirming the window: 2026-10-29 (incident start) through 2027-01-27 (90 days). 

Attached: arcadia-incident-4231-timeline.pdf and arcadia-sig-evidence.xlsx (mapping rows that show the traces are pseudonymized and that request excludes full request bodies). Legal attestation is included in the timeline PDF.

We accept the segmented-retention approach and want the export receipt and signed exception statement at the end of the window.

If you need a signed data processing addendum amendment prior to approval, let us know and we can route that internally.

— Tim
Attachment: arcadia-sig-evidence.xlsx

> Tim — thanks for the details and for the timeline. We can support customer-scoped retention variance...
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Tim Pryor <tim.pryor@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extension for debug trace retention (Arcadia incident #4231)

Tim — I reviewed the artifacts with infra and legal. Summary and next steps: 

1) Approval: Redwood grants a temporary, tenant-scoped retention exception for Arcadia to retain segmented debug traces and tokenized metadata for 90 days (2026-10-29 through 2027-01-27) under the following conditions:
   - Data is stored in a segmented, access-controlled bucket.
   - No downstream analytics, model-training, or external sharing.
   - Access will be logged and limited to named contacts from Arcadia and our forensics SREs.

2) Required deliverables we received and verified: arcadia-incident-4231-timeline.pdf, arcadia-sig-evidence.xlsx (SIG mapping).

3) Attachments delivered: approved-exception-statement.pdf (signed copy), keystore-redaction-runbook.pdf (internal operational runbook describing keystore handling and pseudonymization). We will drop the signed exception to the Drive folder and post an export receipt on 2027-01-28 after the retention window completes.

4) If Arcadia needs a formal amendment to the DPA, please upload the request to the same Drive folder and ask your legal contact to include a point of contact for audit requests.

Ben (cc'd) — please ensure logging for access to the segmented bucket is enabled and that an export receipt is generated on 2027-01-28.

Tim — glad we could move quickly. Let me know if you want a short handoff call with infra; otherwise we will proceed with the segmented retention as described.

— Kimberly Park
Director, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): approved-exception-statement.pdf; keystore-redaction-runbook.pdf
